title: Chain verification does not authenticate statement or justification payloads
evidence: verify_chain hashes stored s_hash/j_hash only (lines 345-374); get_statement/get_justification load payloads without recomputing hashes (497-526). publisher.rs:31-47 verifies then exports these payloads; bindings.rs:35-44 rehydrates them.
trigger: Modify statements.content/modality/obligations_json or justifications.payload_json in an existing database without changing their hash keys.
impact: Replay and export accept altered knowledge while chain verification succeeds; valid JSON tampering is not detected.

title: Nogood primary key prevents revoking the same statement in multiple environments
evidence: atms_nogoods_log declares nogood_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY rather than (nogood_hash, environment_id); assert_nogood unconditionally inserts at 335-338.
trigger: Call assert_nogood(hash, env_a), then assert_nogood(hash, env_b), or repeat the same revocation.
impact: Second revocation returns a SQLite uniqueness error, preventing a per-environment causal revocation record and making retry non-idempotent.

title: Derived assertion and explicit dependency edges commit separately
evidence: assert_derived_knowledge calls assert_knowledge, which commits at 299, before beginning its edge transaction at 312; replay propagation relies on edges at 444-465.
trigger: Process stops or edge insertion/commit fails after assert_knowledge commits and before assert_derived_knowledge commits its edges.
impact: A persisted derived assertion survives without its explicit causal parents, so subsequent revocation closure may omit it.

title: Missing corpus crashes the auditor before it can report absence
evidence: BrainCorpusIndex.__init__ never sets index_duration; index() returns immediately when BRAIN_DIR does not exist (107-109), while run_sharur_100_swarm reads corpus.index_duration unconditionally at 739.
trigger: Run the script in an environment without ~/.gemini/antigravity/brain.
impact: AttributeError prevents the audit from producing a report or explicit missing-input result.

title: OpenAI secret detector uses a literal malformed repetition
evidence: The OpenAI pattern ends in [a-zA-Z0-9]{20,T}; the nonnumeric upper repetition bound is not a valid numeric quantifier. The scanning loop at 154-159 relies on this pattern to increment secret_matches.
trigger: A transcript contains an ordinary sk- prefixed credential.
impact: The scanner misses credentials and reports a misleading zero count. No actual credentials were read or reproduced.

title: Audit emits unconditional compliance verdicts without examining evidence
evidence: Agents 21,22,24-27 and many others assign PASS plus fixed compliance metrics without inspecting corpus data; 592-596 invent nominal entropy when no samples exist. Results feed compile_swarm_sitrep (reporters.py:360-381), which counts PASS and computes exergy_score from that count, then emits the reports at auditor.py:774.
trigger: Run the auditor on a corpus with missing entropy samples or violations of the claimed compliance properties.
impact: Generated forensic reports present untested properties as passing and can mask defects in the audited history. This is an evidence-quality defect, not a claim about physical energy or runtime isolation.

title: Truncated idempotency keys collide in the audit-event primary key
evidence: event_id uses only logical_tick, step_index and idempotency_key[:8]; audit_events.event_id is a global PRIMARY KEY, although the full idempotency key is a distinct UNIQUE field. task_id is omitted.
trigger: Record two distinct keys sharing their first eight characters with the same tick and step, including across tasks.
impact: The second valid event fails its primary-key insert, preventing its checkpoint update.

title: Checkpoint read-modify-write occurs outside the write transaction
evidence: get_checkpoint reads compacted_error_summary before INSERT begins the SQLite transaction; the later ON CONFLICT clause overwrites the complete summary with that stale local list.
trigger: Two CortexWalStore instances read the same task checkpoint, then serialize two successful writes each adding a different error.
impact: The second checkpoint overwrites the first error summary; compaction reads this summary and can omit durable error evidence. The audit_events rows can still retain the original errors.

title: Software-key example certifies hardware-bound attestation
evidence: ScittSigner::new generates an ed25519_dalek SigningKey with OsRng (30-34); sign accesses the in-process key (37-38). The final verdict prints hardware-bound certification at 231 and labels throughput hardware at 216.
trigger: Run the example successfully on software signing alone.
impact: Its output misrepresents software signature round trips as evidence of hardware-bound attestation, without any hardware key provider or hardware authorization step. The finding is limited to example claims.

title: Receipt example accepts missing or malformed required fields
evidence: Parser initializes epoch/hash/timestamp/strings to zero/empty (118-122), silently ignores mismatched types and invalid hash length (124-155), then returns Ok at 158.
trigger: A validly signed CBOR map omits required fields or supplies wrong types.
impact: Verification succeeds and returns default values rather than rejecting an invalid halt receipt; signature integrity alone does not establish the declared payload schema.

title: Autocognition audit asserts checks it never performs
evidence: Generated YAML hardcodes ANNIHILATED_ZERO_CIRCULAR_LOOPS, 0 ruff issues/0 clippy warnings, no orphaned branches and ZERO_NOISE_ACCUMULATION_VERIFIED (185-190). The function only computes transcript metrics then persists the artifact.
trigger: Run run_autocognition_audit in a checkout with lint issues, orphan branches, loops, or no transcript (103-112).
impact: The produced audit declares verified cleanup and tool results without obtaining them, creating false evidence for downstream readers.

title: Explicit conversation selection is ignored in favor of another session
evidence: get_conversation_id evaluates environment values without assigning/returning them at 28; it selects the UUID directory with newest mtime at 43-45, which feeds TRANSCRIPT_PATH at 52.
trigger: Set CONVERSATION_ID or ANTIGRAVITY_CONVERSATION_ID to an active session while another UUID directory has newer mtime.
impact: The audit reads and attributes metrics to a different conversation, breaking its stated active-session scope.

title: Resolve the actual field offset when lowering assignments
evidence: AssignField discards _field and emits FieldPtr offset: 0 at line 56. LayoutEngine already records field_offsets; backend_x86.rs lines 133-139 uses the IR offset to generate LEA.
trigger: Call the exported LoweringContext.lower API with a struct containing multiple fields and an assignment to a non-first field.
impact: Generated IR writes the first field instead of the requested field. This is an acknowledged PoC limitation; no active lowering caller was found within the compiler crate, so no deployed runtime consequence is asserted.

title: PoC prints success after DAG timeout
evidence: Timeout at151-154 breaks without failure flag; unconditional success print and normal main return follow.
trigger: DAG fails to complete within timeout.
impact: Failed PoC is reported successful and exits zero.

title: Non-Darwin arm reports anti-debug protection despite skipping it
evidence: enforce_anti_debug returns immediately when platform != darwin (43–44), yet arm unconditionally sets antidebug_ok=True (69–74). tests/test_c5_memory_shield.py:54 asserts True on every platform.
trigger: Call arm on Linux.
impact: Audit status claims anti-debug protection was armed although no anti-debug mechanism ran.

title: BFT persistence explicitly weakens required durability
evidence: persist_bft_event sets journal_mode=WAL then synchronous=NORMAL before commit; the canonical rules require transactional persistence synchronous=FULL.
trigger: A caller uses persist_bft_event and the host loses power after an acknowledged commit.
impact: The helper provides weaker durability than its BFT persistence contract. No production callers were found in targeted Python searches, so deployed reachability is not established.

title: Native Hamming batch accepts buffers shorter than its stride
evidence: flat_batch joins arbitrary byte strings; q_len alone is passed as the native stride without validating each length. Cross-file utils/void_accel.c:28,34-35 and 58,64-65 read each target at i*len.
trigger: A compatible native library is loaded and a batch member is shorter than query.
impact: Native code reads outside the provided batch buffer; malformed input can crash the process or compute distances from unrelated memory. Native-library loading was not exercised.

title: Synchronous verifiers bypass timeout and block the event loop
evidence: Only coroutine functions enter asyncio.wait_for at lines 42–43; the synchronous branch calls verify_fn(item) directly at line 45. Semaphore capacity is unvalidated at line 35.
trigger: Pass an ordinary blocking verification function, including one that never returns.
impact: timeout_s is ignored and all verification tasks/event-loop work can stall; sync work also runs serially despite the parallel interface.

title: Ablation violation metric is hardcoded for the gated condition
evidence: Conditions 0/1 compute synthetic violations (52/78); condition 2 always emits 0. spinal_gate.py:91-97 samples proposed costs and throws when is_viable is false, which is caught at benchmark lines 103-105.
trigger: The gate encounters a nonviable reading and throws SpinalPainException.
impact: Benchmark records zero violations despite observing a nonviable reading, while baselines use different synthetic definitions. Reported between-condition violation comparison is structurally biased; this is an example benchmark, not a validated empirical agent evaluation.

title: Second-order belief returns the target belief regardless of observer knowledge
evidence: observer_agent is only checked for membership; method returns query_belief(target_agent,...). run_demo consumes it at line 316 and tests/test_doxastic_kripke_engine.py:86 covers only an observer who witnessed the relevant scenario.
trigger: A target privately sees an object move while a different observer is absent; query the absent observer's belief about the target.
impact: Returns the target's updated private belief even though the observer could not know it. The demonstration cannot establish second-order false-belief reasoning. No deployed security consumer was established.

title: Advertised decision latency excludes receipt signing
evidence: t1 is captured before _sign_decision; latency_ns=t1-t0 is reported as decision latency although route signs and constructs the result afterward. The opening claim includes cryptographic receipts and a decision-latency target.
trigger: Use the PoC latency distribution to evaluate the complete route call against its advertised target.
impact: Reported figures omit HMAC/SHA3 work and cannot establish the claimed end-to-end decision latency.

title: Chunk allocation ignores the supplied swarm size
evidence: allocate_chunks loops over self.swarm_size but uses FRAMES_PER_AGENT calculated from the global SWARM_SIZE=10000.
trigger: Instantiate AgencyHypervisor with any non-default swarm_size.
impact: Allocated chunks cover fewer than TOTAL_FRAMES for a smaller swarm or extend beyond it for a larger swarm; the provided default simulation does not exercise this.

title: Concurrent audit appends can fork the hash chain
evidence: Lines 63–71 read the previous tail and compute the next digest before the independent append at lines 73–74; no lock serializes those operations.
trigger: Two pipe_audit processes read the same ledger tail before either appends.
impact: Both new entries name the same predecessor, so the sequential ledger chain breaks under ordinary concurrent auditing; valid activity becomes indistinguishable from a damaged chain. This concerns the audit trail, not a demonstrated execution bypass.

title: Propagate pytest.main exit code from FUZZ workers
evidence: python -c invokes pytest.main(...) without sys.exit; run_cmd uses only subprocess returncode.
trigger: pytest returns a nonzero result without raising out of main.
impact: Worker reports successful parser resilience for failing tests, including collection failures.

title: Synthetic broker labels Python predicates as hardware-attested consensus
evidence: alpha/beta/gamma are Python length and prefix predicates (56-58); simulate_biometric=True creates ATTESTED_NIST_P256. OBSERVED hashes proposed input (74-76), COMMITTED computes a plain hash (78-81). There is no Rust/Lean/Z3 invocation, hardware observation or COSE signature in this file. Targeted references located only its local suite.
trigger: Run the example suite using simulate_biometric=True.
impact: Output claims certification and attestation that the example does not establish; this is an example-evidence defect, not a demonstrated production authorization bypass.

title: Lean verification silently passes when compiler is absent
evidence: test_i4_lean4_standalone_oracle only runs subprocess and checks its result inside if Path(lean_bin).is_file(); there is no else failure or pytest.skip.
trigger: Neither shutil.which("lean") nor /opt/homebrew/bin/lean resolves to an existing compiler file.
impact: The test reports a pass although no Lean verification occurred.

title: Queue acknowledgement guidance reverses the first-call-wins contract
evidence: Lines 95-105 say last call wins and demonstrate ack(); retry() as causing retry. Official Cloudflare documentation https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/configuration/batching-retries/ states the first ack/retry wins and subsequent calls are ignored (retrieved 2026-10-28).
trigger: A consumer follows the example by acknowledging a message and subsequently trying to retry it after discovering a processing failure.
impact: The message remains acknowledged and is not retried, risking loss of intended work. This is documentation/example guidance, not a traced production consumer.

title: Refusal is assigned zero KL without a probability distribution
evidence: Line 54 assigns D_KL=0 to silence/empty output, while lines 48–50 define KL between normalized predictive distributions p and q. An empty output does not define q; zero mass on positive-p outcomes instead gives infinite KL.
trigger: Apply the stated operational signatures to compare a refusing system with a calibrated predictor.
impact: Mathematical audit can score absence of a predictive distribution as perfect calibration; abstention requires a separate coverage/selective-risk metric.

title: BLE discovery filters on characteristic UUID instead of advertised service
evidence: Architecture line 29 identifies service 0000180d... and characteristic 00002a37...; scanner instead searches service_uuids for HR_MEASUREMENT_UUID (00002a37...).
trigger: A standard heart-rate device advertises the 0x180d service described by this same document.
impact: The supplied daemon example does not discover the intended device and returns Emisor no encontrado.
